idea: Petulant toff, early fifties: thinner, nasal, higher-pitched aristocratic voice that cracks into a childish whine. The joke is the tantrum: a grown man in a suit sounding like a spoilt schoolboy, the opposite texture to the steady, warm crew.
tone: A man in his early fifties with a thin, nasal, very posh English aristocratic voice, the drawl of an old Etonian who has never been told no. A government minister throwing a tantrum on his phone in the back of a ministerial car. He starts sharp and clipped, then his voice climbs and cracks into a spoilt, whining shriek on the final words, as if this is the worst day of his life. Close, dry, voice only, natural British drama acting.
